claim: An in-focus data acquisition method for cryo-EM single-particle analysis with the Volta phase plate was previously reported.
source: Previously, we reported an in-focus data acquisition method for cryo-EM single-particle analysis with the Volta phase plate (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).

claim: The hybrid approach of using VPP with defocus simplifies the experiment and increases data acquisition speed.
source: This hybrid approach simplifies the experiment and increases the data acquisition speed.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' experimental observations and methodology described in the manuscript.

claim: The hybrid approach removes the resolution limit inherent to the in-focus method, allowing 3D reconstructions with resolutions better than 3 Å.
source: It also removes the resolution limit inherent to the in-focus method thus allowing 3D reconstructions with resolutions better than 3 Å.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing 2.4 Å resolution achieved in this study compared to 3.2 Å in the previous in-focus method.

claim: The Volta phase plate enables in-focus phase contrast in a transmission electron microscope.
source: The Volta phase plate (VPP) is a device which enables in-focus phase contrast in a transmission electron microscope (TEM) (Danev et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Danev et al., 2014).

claim: The VPP is the first phase-plate-type device to reach near-atomic resolutions in single particle cryo-EM.
source: It is the first phase-plate-type device to reach near-atomic resolutions in single particle cryo-EM (Chua et al., 2016; Danev and Baumeister, 2016; Khoshouei et al., 2016a, 2016b).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work demonstrating near-atomic resolution with VPP.

claim: Small, heterogeneous and/or flexible molecules are generally difficult to solve by the traditional defocus phase contrast method.
source: Small, heterogeneous and/or flexible molecules are generally difficult to solve by the traditional defocus phase contrast (DPC) method (Cheng et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2015).

claim: The VPP improves image contrast.
source: The VPP improves image contrast and thus could help with solving the structures of such 'difficult' samples.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the VPP and is supported by visual evidence in the figures.

claim: The in-focus method requires very accurate focusing which complicates and slows down data acquisition.
source: It requires very accurate focusing which complicates and slows down the data acquisition.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience with the in-focus method.

claim: The achievable resolution with the in-focus method is limited by the spherical aberration of the objective lens to ~3 Å.
source: Furthermore, the achievable resolution is limited by the spherical aberration of the objective lens to ~3 Å.
evidence: The claim is based on theoretical understanding of electron optics and is supported by the experimental results showing 3.2 Å resolution in the previous in-focus dataset.

claim: 3D reconstruction software did not support VPP phase shift in the contrast transfer function at the time of the initial report.
source: At the time of our initial report the 3D reconstruction software did not yet support VPP phase shift (PS) in the contrast transfer function (CTF).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the state of software development at the time.

claim: Support for VPP phase shift in CTF was implemented in 3D reconstruction software, enabling the present work.
source: In the meantime, such support was implemented which enabled the present work.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' knowledge of software updates and their ability to perform the current analysis.

claim: The hybrid approach combines the VPP with a small amount of defocus.
source: Here, we present a hybrid approach which combines the VPP with a small amount of defocus.
evidence: The claim describes the methodology used in this study.

claim: The hybrid approach solves the resolution limit issue of the in-focus approach by enabling CTF fitting and correction.
source: It simplifies the data acquisition to a level similar to DPC and solves the resolution limit issue of the in-focus approach by enabling CTF fitting and correction.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results showing improved resolution with CTF correction.

claim: Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome was used as a test sample in the previous in-focus cryo-EM report with VPP.
source: In our report on in-focus cryo-EM with the VPP we used Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome as a test sample (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The same sample (Thermoplasma acidophilum 20S proteasome) was used in this study for consistency and continuation.
source: Here, we used the same sample for consistency and continuation.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental design choice made by the authors.

claim: Acquiring images with defocus is easier and faster because defocus and astigmatism can be fitted and corrected a posteriori.
source: Acquiring images with defocus is easier and faster because the defocus and astigmatism can be fitted and corrected a posteriori.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience and understanding of the methodology.

claim: The VPP provides low frequency contrast which allows the use of defocus values smaller than those typically used in DPC.
source: The VPP provides low frequency contrast which allows the use of defocus values smaller than those typically used in DPC.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of VPP and the experimental approach used in this study.

claim: Because of the low defocus, the defocused VPP images look similar to in-focus images.
source: Because of the low defocus the images (Figure 1A) look similar to in-focus images (Figure 4A in Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by visual comparison of images in Figure 1A and reference to a previous figure.

claim: The power spectrum of defocused VPP images clearly shows the effect of defocus with characteristic CTF rings (Thon rings).
source: The power spectrum in Figure 1B, however, clearly shows the effect of defocus with characteristic CTF rings (Thon rings).
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1B.

claim: Fitting the CTFs of VPP data requires an additional phase shift parameter.
source: Fitting the CTFs of VPP data requires an additional PS parameter (Rohou and Grigorieff, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work describing CTF fitting methodology.

claim: CTF fits provide a quantitative measure of the behavior of the VPP.
source: Such fits provide a quantitative measure of the behavior of the VPP.
evidence: The claim is based on the methodology used to analyze VPP behavior.

claim: The VPP was advanced to a new position every 1.5 hr (every ~40 images, total dose on the VPP ~50 nC).
source: The VPP was advanced to a new position every 1.5 hr (every ~40 images, total dose on the VPP ~50 nC).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental protocol used in data acquisition.

claim: After each advance of the VPP, the phase shift drops abruptly to a low value (<0.2 π) and starts to gradually build up again.
source: After each advance the PS drops abruptly to a low value (<0.2 π) and starts to gradually build up again.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The phase shift distribution has a maximum at ~0.6 π with a relatively small number of micrographs exhibiting low (<0.2 π) or high (>0.8 π) phase shift.
source: The distribution has a maximum at ~0.6 π with a relatively small number of micrographs exhibiting low (<0.2 π) or high (>0.8 π) PS.
evidence: The claim is supported by the histogram shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The evolving phase shift of the VPP is an advantage for single particle analysis because it moves the positions of the CTF zeros.
source: The evolving PS of the VPP is an advantage for single particle analysis because it moves the positions of the CTF zeros thus mitigating the need to vary the defocus, which is necessary with DPC.
evidence: The claim is based on theoretical understanding of CTF behavior and its implications for data collection.

claim: With the VPP, datasets can be collected with a single, low defocus value.
source: With the VPP, datasets can be collected with a single, low defocus value.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental approach used in this study and the properties of VPP.

claim: The VPP used in this work exhibited more phase shift than in the original VPP paper.
source: In this work (Figure 1C) as well as in the previous report (Figure 3 in Danev and Baumeister, 2016) the VPP exhibited more PS than in the original VPP paper (Figure 1C in Danev et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of data from different studies.

claim: There is some variation in the phase shift magnitude between different areas on the phase plate.
source: In addition, there is some variation in the PS magnitude between different areas on the phase plate (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: It is advantageous to have a VPP with slower phase shift development because this allows collection of more images at each position.
source: In practice, it is advantageous to have a VPP with slower PS development because this allows collection of more images at each position.
evidence: The claim is based on practical considerations for data collection efficiency.

claim: The heater used in the original VPP paper was a pre-production prototype and the phase plate was homemade.
source: The heater used in the original VPP paper (Danev et al., 2014) was a pre-production prototype and the phase plate was homemade thus the production versions used in this work seem to exhibit a faster PS development.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the equipment used in different studies.

claim: The production versions of VPP used in this work exhibit faster phase shift development than the prototype.
source: The heater used in the original VPP paper (Danev et al., 2014) was a pre-production prototype and the phase plate was homemade thus the production versions used in this work seem to exhibit a faster PS development.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of VPP behavior across different studies.

claim: The variation of phase shift across VPP areas could indicate a local variation in the quality of the amorphous carbon film.
source: The variation of the PS across VPP areas could indicate a local variation in the quality of the amorphous carbon film.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the observed phase shift variation.

claim: The observed factors do not prevent the collection of high quality data with VPP.
source: Overall, those factors do not prevent the collection of high quality data, as illustrated by the results presented here, but there is definitely room for improvement and we hope that manufacturers will take those observations into account when they develop future versions of the hardware.
evidence: The claim is supported by the high-resolution results obtained in this study.

claim: The target defocus was changed approximately halfway through the dataset acquisition from 500 nm to 300 nm.
source: Approximately halfway through the dataset acquisition we changed the target defocus from 500 nm to 300 nm to evaluate the performance at different defocus values.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental protocol and is supported by Figure 1E.

claim: The measured defocus has periodic oscillations with ~16 image period, probably caused by local variations in the slant of the support film (waviness).
source: The measured defocus has periodic oscillations, with ~16 image period, probably caused by local variations in the slant of the support film (waviness), which can introduce a defocus difference between the focusing and acquisition positions.
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figure 1E and speculative interpretation of the cause.

claim: The distribution of the 300 nm target defocus data is wider than the 500 nm one.
source: The distribution of the 300 nm target defocus data is wider than the 500 nm one but this seems to be caused by the systematic defocus oscillations and not by random focusing errors (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the histograms shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The 300 nm target defocus had a practical disadvantage in that fitting the CTFs of micrographs with defocus <300 nm was difficult.
source: The 300 nm target defocus had a practical disadvantage in that fitting the CTFs of micrographs with defocus <300 nm was difficult because the CTF has fewer rings and their period is similar to power spectrum features, such as the amorphous ice ring at ~3.7 Å.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience with data processing.

claim: In practice, the 500 nm defocus was more robust and easier to process than 300 nm defocus.
source: In practice, the 500 nm defocus was more robust and easier to process.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience with data processing.

claim: High phase shift (>0.8 π) is undesirable because it causes CTF artifacts and reduces the quality of the data.
source: High PS (>0.8 π) is undesirable because it causes CTF artifacts and thus reduces the quality of the data.
evidence: The claim is based on theoretical understanding of CTF behavior and supported by the data analysis.

claim: Images with low phase shift (0.1 π) have lower contrast than images with optimal phase shift.
source: The image on the left has a low PS (0.1 π) and consequently lower contrast.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 2A.

claim: Images close to the optimal phase shift of 0.5 π have good contrast and the best appearance.
source: The middle image is close to the optimal PS of 0.5 π and has good contrast and the best appearance.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 2A.

claim: Images acquired with high phase shift of 0.9 π look 'blurry'.
source: The image on the right was acquired with a high PS of 0.9 π and looks 'blurry'.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 2A.

claim: The blurriness in high phase shift images is caused by an extra CTF maximum at very low spatial frequencies.
source: The blurriness is caused by an extra CTF maximum at very low spatial frequencies illustrated in Figure 2B.
evidence: The claim is based on theoretical analysis of CTF behavior shown in Figure 2B.

claim: It is difficult to predict the exact shape or size of the central spot of the VPP.
source: In practice, it is difficult to predict the exact shape or size of the central spot of the VPP.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience with VPP.

claim: Factors such as specimen charging, specimen thickness and beam drift could cause the central beam to change its shape or move on the phase plate.
source: Factors such as specimen charging, specimen thickness and beam drift could cause the central beam to change its shape or move on the phase plate and thus modify the central spot.
evidence: The claim is a speculative explanation based on known physical phenomena.

claim: The central spot of the VPP was approximated with a Gaussian function which has only one parameter – the size of the spot.
source: We approximated the central spot of the VPP with a Gaussian function which has only one parameter – the size of the spot.
evidence: The claim describes the modeling approach used in the analysis.

claim: The Gaussian approximation is a simple model which, although not accurate in every case, provides a satisfactory simulation of the VPP central spot.
source: This is a simple model which, although not accurate in every case, provides a satisfactory simulation of a rather unpredictable function.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' evaluation of their modeling approach.

claim: Particles with low (<0.2 π) and high (>0.8 π) phase shifts were predominantly rejected during 3D classification.
source: Particles with low (<0.2 π) and high (>0.8 π) PSs were predominantly rejected indicating that such particles had low correspondence with the reference.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There was no correlation between defocus and particle retention.
source: There was no correlation between defocus and particle retention.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the data processing results.

claim: The first few images after moving the VPP to a new position have a low phase shift which quickly develops.
source: The first few images after moving the VPP to a new position have a low PS which quickly develops (Figure 3 in Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work showing this behavior.

claim: In images taken shortly after moving the VPP, there may be noticeable phase shift evolution throughout the multiframe movie.
source: In those images there may be noticeable PS evolution throughout the multiframe movie.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the known behavior of VPP phase shift development.

claim: The CTF model can be modified to include the central VPP spot to improve handling of high phase shift images.
source: For high PS images, the CTF model can, in principle, be modified to include the central VPP spot which should improve their handling.
evidence: The claim is a speculative suggestion for future improvement.

claim: It is best to avoid both low and high phase shift images through an improved data acquisition strategy.
source: However, it is best to avoid both low and high PS images which could be achieved through an improved data acquisition strategy.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' analysis of data quality at different phase shifts.

claim: An optimal data acquisition solution would incorporate phase shift monitoring through on-the-fly CTF fitting.
source: An optimal solution would be to incorporate PS monitoring in the automated data acquisition software through on-the-fly CTF fitting of the acquired images.
evidence: The claim is a speculative suggestion for future improvement.

claim: The reconstruction reached a resolution of 2.4 Å according to the gold-standard FSC 0.143 criterion.
source: The reconstruction reached a resolution of 2.4 Å according to the gold-standard Fourier shell correlation (FSC) 0.143 criterion (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the FSC plot shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The visibility of primary structure features, such as holes in tyrosine and phenylalanine rings, is in accordance with the 2.4 Å resolution estimate.
source: The visibility of primary structure features, such as the holes in the tyrosine and phenylalanine rings (Figure 3B), is in accordance with that estimate.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 3B.

claim: The local resolution varies between 2.2 Å and 2.6 Å.
source: The local resolution varies between 2.2 Å and 2.6 Å (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the local resolution map shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is significant improvement in resolution compared to the previous in-focus dataset at 3.2 Å.
source: The significant improvement in resolution compared to our previous in-focus dataset, at 3.2 Å (Danev and Baumeister, 2016), confirms the effectiveness of the CTF correction.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of resolution values from this study and prior work.

claim: The resolution improvement is consistent throughout the particle number range with a significant extension towards low particle numbers.
source: The resolution improvement is consistent throughout the particle number range with a significant extension towards low particle numbers.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The defocused dataset was collected with a smaller pixel size (1.054 Å vs 1.35 Å previously) and in super-resolution mode of the K2 camera.
source: The improvement is also a result of the fact that the defocused dataset was collected with a smaller pixel size (1.054 Å vs 1.35 Å previously) and in super-resolution mode of the K2 camera.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental parameters used in data collection.

claim: The B-factor calculated from the particle number vs resolution plot was 103 Å².
source: The B-factor calculated as twice the slope of the fit (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003) was 103 Å2.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data and analysis shown in Figure 3F.

claim: A DPC dataset was not collected in this work because the main goal was to explore the capabilities of the VPP.
source: In this work we did not collect a DPC dataset because our main goal was to explore the capabilities of the VPP.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental design choice made by the authors.

claim: With an 'easy' specimen such as the 20S proteasome, DPC would be expected to produce very similar results to those of the VPP.
source: We expect that with an 'easy' specimen, such as the 20S proteasome, DPC would have produced very similar results to those of the VPP.
evidence: The claim is a speculative expectation based on the nature of the sample.

claim: MotionCor2 performs movie frame alignment with local motion tracking and dose-weighting.
source: It performs movie frame alignment with local motion tracking and dose-weighting.
evidence: The claim describes the functionality of the MotionCor2 software.

claim: MotionCor2 preprocessing provides similar performance gains to particle polishing in Relion but is more efficient in terms of computation and storage space.
source: Such preprocessing provides similar performance gains to particle polishing in Relion (Scheres, 2014) but is more efficient in terms of computation and storage space.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' comparison of the two methods.

claim: The MotionCor2 workflow result was virtually identical to particle polishing in terms of resolution (2.42 Å MotionCor2 vs 2.36 Å polishing).
source: The results was, for all practical purposes, virtually identical to that from particle polishing both in terms of resolution (2.42 Å MotionCor2 vs 2.36 Å polishing) and B-factor (85 Å2 MotionCor2 vs 74 Å2 polishing).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of results from the two processing workflows.

claim: The MotionCor2 workflow result was virtually identical to particle polishing in terms of B-factor (85 Å² MotionCor2 vs 74 Å² polishing).
source: The results was, for all practical purposes, virtually identical to that from particle polishing both in terms of resolution (2.42 Å MotionCor2 vs 2.36 Å polishing) and B-factor (85 Å2 MotionCor2 vs 74 Å2 polishing).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of results from the two processing workflows.

claim: The authors now use the MotionCor2 workflow for most of their projects because of its simplicity, speed and comparable performance.
source: Because of its simplicity, speed and comparable performance, nowadays we use the MotionCor2 workflow for most of our projects.
evidence: The claim describes the authors' current practice based on their evaluation of the method.

claim: The use of VPP with defocus simplifies data acquisition and improves acquisition speed.
source: In summary, the use of VPP with defocus simplifies the data acquisition and improves the acquisition speed.
evidence: The claim summarizes the practical advantages demonstrated in the study.

claim: The evolving phase shift of the VPP allows the use of a constant, low target defocus.
source: The evolving PS of the VPP allows the use of a constant, low target defocus.
evidence: The claim is based on the observed behavior of VPP and its implications for data collection.

claim: 500 nm is a good practical defocus value because it ensures reliable CTF fits with some margin for random or systematic focusing errors.
source: In our experience, 500 nm is a good practical value because it ensures reliable CTF fits with some margin for random or systematic focusing errors.
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' practical experience with data collection and processing.

claim: Future modifications of data acquisition software to include on-the-fly CTF fitting, phase shift monitoring and VPP pre-irradiation would improve performance.
source: Future modifications of the data acquisition software, to include on-the-fly CTF fitting, PS monitoring and VPP pre-irradiation, would improve the performance by preventing the collection of low and high PS images.
evidence: The claim is a speculative suggestion for future improvement.

claim: The VPP is not limited in resolution and matches the state of the art of DPC for 'easy' samples such as the 20S proteasome.
source: Here, we demonstrated that the VPP is not limited in resolution and matches the state of the art of DPC for 'easy' samples, such as the 20S proteasome.
evidence: The claim is supported by the high-resolution results obtained in this study.

claim: The real performance advantage of the VPP needs further exploration using 'difficult' samples, such as small, flexible and/or heterogeneous samples.
source: The real performance advantage of the VPP needs further exploration using 'difficult' samples, such as small, flexible and/or heterogeneous samples.
evidence: The claim is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Cryo-samples were prepared as described in the previous report (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
source: Cryo-samples were prepared as described previously (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim references the sample preparation method from prior work.

claim: Data was collected on an FEI Titan Krios electron microscope operated at 300 kV.
source: The data was collected on an FEI Ttian Krios (FEI, Hillsboro, OR) electron microscope operated at 300 kV and equipped with a Gatan GIF Quantum energy filter and a Gatan K2 Summit direct detection camera (Gatan, Pleasanton, CA).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental equipment used.

claim: The microscope was equipped with a Gatan GIF Quantum energy filter and a Gatan K2 Summit direct detection camera.
source: The data was collected on an FEI Ttian Krios (FEI, Hillsboro, OR) electron microscope operated at 300 kV and equipped with a Gatan GIF Quantum energy filter and a Gatan K2 Summit direct detection camera (Gatan, Pleasanton, CA).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental equipment used.

claim: The data was acquired automatically with SerialEM software.
source: The data was acquired automatically with SerialEM software (Mastronarde, 2005).
evidence: The claim describes the data acquisition method and cites the software.

claim: The data acquisition speed was ~27 images/hour, comparable to that of the previously collected in-focus dataset.
source: The data acquisition speed was ~27 images/hour, comparable to that of the previously collected in-focus dataset (Danev and Baumeister, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by measurement of acquisition speed and comparison to prior work.

claim: The throughput did not improve despite simplified focusing because of the use of super-resolution mode of the K2 camera which added ~50 s to the time required to process and save movie frames.
source: The throughput did not improve, despite simplified focusing, because of the use of super-resolution mode of the K2 camera which added ~50 s to the time required to process and save the movie frames.
evidence: The claim explains why the expected throughput improvement was not observed.

claim: The movies were saved as dark-subtracted but non-gain-normalized LZW compressed TIFF files which significantly reduced their size (~220 MB/movie).
source: The movies were saved as dark-subtracted but non-gain-normalized LZW compressed TIFF files which significantly reduced their size (~220 MB/movie).
evidence: The claim describes the data storage method and its effect on file size.

claim: The dataset consisted of 468 micrographs, 41 (9%) of which were rejected after visual inspection, leaving 427 micrographs for processing.
source: The dataset consisted of 468 micrographs, 41 (9%) of which were rejected after visual inspection, leaving 427 micrographs for processing.
evidence: The claim describes the dataset composition and quality control.

claim: The initial dataset of 145,870 particles was subjected to 3D refinement with D7 symmetry which reached a resolution of 2.6 Å with a B-factor of 111 Å².
source: The initial dataset of 145,870 particles was subjected to a 3D refinement with D7 symmetry which reached a resolution of 2.6 Å with a B-factor of 111 Å2.
evidence: The claim describes the initial processing results.

claim: The best 3D class, containing 93,596 particles (64% of the dataset), was 3D refined producing the final reconstruction with a resolution of 2.4 Å and a B-factor of 74 Å².
source: The best class, containing 93,596 particles (64% of the dataset), was 3D refined producing the final reconstruction with a resolution of 2.4 Å and a B-factor of 74 Å2.
evidence: The claim describes the final processing results after classification.

claim: One of the 3D classes showed structure deformation in the form of separation between the top and bottom halves of the 20S, probably due to incomplete assembly of some particles.
source: The other 3D classes refined to much lower resolutions with one of them showing some structure deformation in the form of separation between the top and bottom halves of the 20S. This was probably due to an incomplete assembly of some particles rather than being a valid functional state.
evidence: The claim describes an observation from 3D classification and provides a speculative interpretation.

claim: For the MotionCor2 based reconstruction, 48 micrographs with estimated CTF resolution of less than 3.5 Å were discarded, leaving 379 micrographs for processing.
source: Micrographs with estimated CTF resolution of less than 3.5 Å were discarded (48 micrographs) leaving 379 micrographs for processing.
evidence: The claim describes the quality control criteria and dataset composition for the MotionCor2 workflow.

claim: 83,127 particles from the best 3D class were 3D refined producing a final reconstruction with a resolution of 2.4 Å and a B-factor of 85 Å² using the MotionCor2 workflow.
source: 83,127 particles from the best 3D class were 3D refined producing a final reconstruction with a resolution of 2.4 Å and a B-factor of 85 Å2.
evidence: The claim describes the final processing results using the MotionCor2 workflow.

claim: The reconstructed 3D density maps were deposited to the EMDataBank with accession codes EMD-3455 and EMD-3456.
source: The reconstructed 3D density maps from the Relion particle polishing and MotionCor2 data processing workflows were deposited to the EMDataBank with accession codes EMD-3455 and EMD-3456 respectively.
evidence: The claim provides information about data deposition.

claim: The dataset was deposited to the Electron Microscopy Pilot Image Archive with accession code EMPIAR-10078.
source: The dataset was deposited to the Electron Microscopy Pilot Image Archive with accession code EMPIAR-10078.
evidence: The claim provides information about data deposition.

claim: The power spectrum was calculated as the sum of the power spectra of individual movie frames to enhance the visibility of Thon rings.
source: To enhance the visibility of Thon rings, the power spectrum was calculated as the sum of the power spectra of individual movie frames (McMullan et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim describes the method used to generate Figure 1B and cites the methodology.

claim: The CTF model used in data processing is that of an ideal phase plate with a delta-function-like central spot.
source: The CTF model used in data processing is that of an ideal phase plate with a delta-function-like central spot (black dashed line).
evidence: The claim describes the theoretical model used in data processing, illustrated in Figure 2B.

claim: The large deviation between the practical and theoretical CTFs means that high phase shift images are not handled optimally during processing.
source: The large deviation between the practical and the theoretical CTFs (pink area in Figure 2B) means that high PS images are not handled optimally during processing.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of theoretical and practical CTF models shown in Figure 2B.
